source.question: Which wells need attention right now, and why?

note: Reviewed (Nov 1, new questions and synthetic field): fair, or strict at the cost of a round, not of the run.

submission.summary: P-1 needs immediate attention because its water cut is about 90% and it makes only about 146 Sm3/d oil with the choke already fully open at 100%, so water has taken its liquid capacity. P-2 needs watching as its water cut rose from about 12.5% to 33% during 2020 and is still climbing. Injector I-2 has been stopped since 2019-08-31, leaving only I-1 injecting, while P-3 and P-4 remain steady low-water producers.

findings.claim: P-1 is on alarm with a water cut of 90.3% at 2020-12-31 and an oil rate of about 146 Sm3/d, down 12.5% over the last 90 days.
findings.detail: field_screen as_of 2020-12-31: P-1 water_cut 0.903 alarm since 2019-05-31, oil_rate 145.97 Sm3/d, uptime 0.9901, oil_rate_change_90d -0.125. Monthly Dec 2020 oil_rate_per_producing_day 140.79 Sm3/d, water_cut 0.903.

findings.claim: P-1's liquid capacity is full: the choke has been at 100% since 2018-03 and liquid rate fell to 1 822 Sm3/d in 2020 from 2 976 Sm3/d in 2018.
findings.detail: waterflood by_year: 2018 liquid_rate 2976 choke 100.0 water_cut 0.8616, 2020 liquid_rate 1822 choke 100.0 water_cut 0.9029. Monthly liquid rates 1451 Sm3/d Dec 2020. WOR trend 2018-01 to 2020-12 r2 0.75, already passed water cuts 0.80 and 0.90, with 192,412 Sm3 oil left before 0.95.

findings.claim: P-1's oil decline is steep on a harmonic fit with an initial rate of 1 464 Sm3/d from 2017-08-13, and its downhole gauge has read zero since 2018-04-10.
findings.detail: fit_decline P-1 window 2017-08-13 to 2020-12-31 best harmonic qi 1464 Sm3/d, di 2.47 per year, b 1.0, r2_log 0.9723, n 1206. detect_events gauge_failure bhp 0 on 997 days from 2018-04-10 with 261,474 Sm3 oil produced, last good 240.2 on 2018-04-09. Oil regime change around 2017-08-13 weekly mean 2865 -> 399 Sm3/d (-86%).

findings.claim: P-2's water cut has risen quickly in 2020 to 32.6% in December from 12.5% in January, with a 2020 average of 23.0%.
findings.detail: production_monthly P-2 2020-01 water_cut 0.1246, 2020-12 water_cut 0.3256, oil_rate_per_producing_day 361.67 -> 295.93 Sm3/d. waterflood by_year 2020 water_cut 0.2297 liquid 417.17 choke 40.0. No WOR trend yet (0 months with WOR>=1).

findings.claim: P-2's earlier oil drop around 2018-11-11 averaged 74% less after than before, but the choke was cut from 70% to 40% at the same time.
findings.detail: detect_events P-2 regime around 2018-11-11 before_mean 1426 after_mean 368.95 relative_change -0.7413 across_before 786.42 across_after 463.29 change_across -0.4109 choke_before 70.0 choke_after 40.0 choke_moved true. Subsequent water_cut regimes 2019-09-29 and 2020-05-24.

findings.claim: Injector I-2 has injected no water since 2019-08-31, leaving field injection to I-1 at about 3 150 Sm3/d.
findings.detail: field_screen I-2 water_inj 0.0 since 2019-08-31 note stopped. I-1 water_inj 3150 Sm3/d. cum injected I-1 6,668,065 vs I-2 5,053,468. Field voidage replacement_ratio 0.78 in 2020, 1.04 in 2019.

findings.claim: P-3 and P-4 remain low-water producers with water cuts of 1% and 2% and steady hyperbolic declines, needing no immediate action.
findings.detail: field_screen P-3 oil_rate 258.25 water_cut 0.01, P-4 oil_rate 795.49 water_cut 0.02. fit_decline P-3 hyperbolic qi 1803 di 0.5531 b 0.3049 r2_log 0.9925, P-4 hyperbolic qi 1593 di 0.4813 b 0.302 r2_log 0.9492. waterflood by_year 2020 P-3 water_cut 0.01 liquid 295.44, P-4 water_cut 0.02 liquid 932.23.

issues.text: downhole pressure gauge reads 0 (997 days, 261,474 Sm3 oil produced without pressure data): a monitoring gap, the well flows on

result.levels: alarm: act now; caution: watch; note: for the record

result.summary: 30-day median water_cut first goes above 0.05 on 2016-08-02, 19 months after first oil.
water_cut shifts around 2017-03-19: weekly mean 0.0487 -> 0.468 (+0.42) from the period before to the period after; across the change itself, 4 weeks each side, 0.24 -> 0.28 (+0.04).
30-day median water_cut first goes above 0.5 on 2017-08-10, 31 months after first oil.

oil_rate shifts around 2017-08-13: weekly mean 2,865 -> 399 (-86%) from the period before to the period after; across the change itself, 4 weeks each side, 1,572 -> 1,435 (-9%); the choke stayed about the same (77 -> 81%).
water_cut shifts around 2017-11-12: weekly mean 0.468 -> 0.875 (+0.41) from the period before to the period after; across the change itself, 4 weeks each side, 0.65 -> 0.69 (+0.04).
30-day median water_cut first goes above 0.8 on 2018-03-20, 38 months after first oil.
bhp_bar reads 0 on 997 days from 2018-04-10 to 2020-12-31 while the well kept flowing on 972 days (261,474 Sm3 oil): a sensor failure, not a pressure collapse. Last good reading: 240.2 on 2018-04-09.
Shut in for 14 days from 2019-06-03. Oil rate 291 -> 283 Sm3/d (-3%) after restart. Same time as P-2, P-3, P-4 (field-wide).

oil_rate shifts around 2018-11-11: weekly mean 1,426 -> 369 (-74%) from the period before to the period after; across the change itself, 4 weeks each side, 786 -> 463 (-41%); the choke was cut at the same time (70 -> 40%), so part of the change is the operator's, not the reservoir's.
Shut in for 14 days from 2019-06-03. Oil rate 414 -> 405 Sm3/d (-2%) after restart. Same time as P-1, P-3, P-4 (field-wide).
30-day median water_cut first goes above 0.05 on 2019-07-22, 53 months after first oil.
water_cut shifts around 2019-09-29: weekly mean 0.0159 -> 0.13 (+0.11) from the period before to the period after; across the change itself, 4 weeks each side, 0.07 -> 0.08 (+0.01).
water_cut shifts around 2020-05-24: weekly mean 0.13 -> 0.272 (+0.14) from the period before to the period after; across the change itself, 4 weeks each side, 0.19 -> 0.21 (+0.02).
Shut in for 14 days from 2019-06-03. Oil rate 426 -> 404 Sm3/d (-5%) after restart. Same time as P-1, P-2, P-4 (field-wide).
Shut in for 14 days from 2019-06-03. Oil rate 1,482 -> 1,411 Sm3/d (-5%) after restart. Same time as P-1, P-2, P-3 (field-wide).

result.notes: WOR = water/oil by month; the trend is log10(WOR) against cumulative oil, fitted on up to 36 recent months with WOR >= 1. The water cuts in to_limits are reference points, not an economic limit: the data holds no costs or prices, so remaining_oil_sm3 says how much oil is left before each, not whether it pays. field_voidage: replacement_ratio is injection over voidage at reservoir conditions (Bo 1.385 m3/Sm3 from PUD p.20, low/high with Bo 1.5/1.27; Bw 1; above the bubble point, so no free gas); surface_ratio is the same in surface volumes, which overstates replacement.

result.no_trend: too few months with WOR >= 1 (water cut 0.5) to fit a trend: 0, need 12

arguments.sql: SELECT well, date, water_inj_sm3, on_stream_hrs FROM production_daily WHERE well IN ('I-1','I-2') AND date >= '2019-07-01' ORDER BY well, date LIMIT 200
SELECT well, sum(oil_sm3) oil, sum(water_sm3) water, sum(water_inj_sm3) inj FROM production_daily WHERE date >= '2020-01-01' GROUP BY well
